children: The benchmark indices fell around 1 percent on September 9, extending their downtrend for the third consecutive session. Market breadth remained negative, with about 1,986 shares declining against 1,272 advancing shares on the NSE. The market is likely to see consolidation with a negative bias. Here are some short-term trading ideas to consider:
Rupak De, Senior Technical Analyst at LKP Securities

Urban Company has seen a sigh of relief on Wednesday following a few days of decline on the daily timeframe, suggesting an initial sign of recovery. On the hourly chart, the price has recovered above the 50EMA, indicating a possible improvement in the trend. The hourly RSI is in a bullish crossover.

Besides, the stock has found support around the low of the previous congestion zone and has recovered from those levels. In the near term, the trend might remain positive, with the stock having the potential to rise towards Rs 185. On the lower end, support is placed at Rs 167.
Inox Wind has moved up after a few days of consolidation, pointing towards a rise in bullish sentiment. Besides, the stock is sustaining above the 20EMA on the daily timeframe.

The price has also risen after forming a positive divergence, indicating improving momentum. Overall, the sentiment looks positive for the stock, with the potential to rise towards Rs 81 in the short term. On the lower end, support is placed at Rs 76.
DLF has fallen from its recent consolidation, suggesting a rise in pessimism around the stock. The price has slipped below the critical moving average on the daily timeframe.

The RSI is in a bearish crossover and continues to fall, indicating weakening momentum. The weakness might persist in the short term, with a possible downside towards Rs 645. On the higher end, resistance is placed at Rs 670, above which the trend might improve. Sell DLF September Futures around Rs 662.
Sudeep Shah - Head of Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities
CG Power and Industrial Solutions | CMP: Rs 926.95

CG Power and Industrial Solutions was consolidating in the Rs 916–860 zone since August 5 before witnessing a decisive breakout and closing higher. The stock is now trading above its key short and long-term moving averages, indicating a strengthening bullish setup.

The RSI has turned higher and moved marginally above the 60 mark, signalling renewed bullish momentum. Meanwhile, the DI lines have widened further, with DI+ firmly placed above DI- on the ADX indicator, highlighting the increasing dominance of bulls.

Sustained trading above the breakout zone could pave the way for further upside, with the overall technical setup remaining firmly positive in the near term. Hence, the accumulation is recommended in the zone of Rs 920-930 with a stop-loss of Rs 890. On the upside, it is likely to test the level of Rs 995 in the short term.

Apollo Hospitals has witnessed a decisive breakout from a symmetrical triangle pattern on the daily chart, signalling a potential resumption of the uptrend. The breakout is backed by a healthy rise in volumes over the last three sessions, adding conviction to the move.

Momentum indicators have also turned supportive, with the RSI breaking above its horizontal trendline resistance, indicating renewed buying momentum. The DI+ has crossed above DI- on the ADX indicator, suggesting that bulls are gaining control over sellers.

Further strengthening the setup, the MACD line has crossed above the zero line, reinforcing the positive bias and indicating scope for further upside in the near term. Hence, the accumulation is recommended in the zone of Rs 8,880-8,960 with a stop-loss of Rs 8,600. On the upside, it is likely to test the level of Rs 9,585 in the short term.
Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone | CMP: Rs 1,775

Adani Ports was consolidating in the Rs 1,724–1,593 zone since the start of August. Following the sharp 6.70 percent decline on August 31, which pushed the stock below its 200-day EMA, the stock has staged a strong rebound and decisively broken above the upper end of the consolidation range. The breakout is supported by a healthy rise in volumes, adding conviction to the move.

The RSI is rising, indicating renewed bullish momentum, while the stock has also closed above the upper Bollinger Band, a phenomenon often associated with the early stages of a strong trend. Sustained momentum could pave the way for further upside. Hence, the accumulation is recommended in the zone of Rs 1,750-1,770 with a stop-loss of Rs 1,700. On the upside, it is likely to test the level of Rs 1,895 in the short term.
